about: The phrase “Cálicem salutáris” comes from Psalm 115:4 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 116:13 in Hebrew): “I will take the chalice of salvation, and call upon the name of the Lord.” The closing petition returns to the biblical “odor suavitátis”, a description of an offering made to the Lord (Lev 4:31).

s01.narrative: The priest takes the chalice and offers it, saying:

s02.translation: We offer Thee, Lord, the chalice of salvation, beseeching Thy clemency: that it may go up with a sweet fragrance in the sight of Thy divine majesty, for our salvation and that of the whole world. Amen.

w005.function: Genitive of the neuter noun “salutáre”, dependent on “cálicem” (w004).

w007.function: A participle referring to the unexpressed subject of “Offérimus” (w001).

w016.function: Feminine ablative agreeing with “salúte” (w020), not a neuter plural.

w020.function: Both “nostra” and “totíus mundi” qualify this noun.

w024.function: Subjunctive after “ut” (w009), with the chalice as its subject.
